title: Shadow Traffic: define capacity budget + load test plan; alerts and runbook readiness
creator: Sean Gallagher
description:
Objective
Define safe capacity budgets and an executable load test plan for Shadow Traffic (shadow runner + queue), and establish paging/alerting + runbook readiness for Beta.

Scope
1) Capacity budgets
- Define global + per-region budgets for shadow executions that ensure primary-path SLOs are not impacted.
- Define default safe sampling caps per route and per customer tier.
- Define queue/backpressure guardrails and explicit drop behavior (shadow-only drops acceptable; must be observable).

2) Load test plan
- Write and execute a load test matrix across sampling %, concurrency, regions, and shadow target types.
- Validate that primary p99 latency and error rate are unchanged within budget during shadow load.
- Validate queue depth stability and expected drop behavior under overload.

3) Alerts + dashboards
- Alerts for queue depth growth, sustained shadow error rate, and shadow drop counts.
- Alert thresholds tuned for actionable paging (no noisy pages for expected shadow-only failures).
- Confirm dashboards exist and are linked from runbook.

4) Runbook readiness
- Ensure kill switch workflow is documented and verified end-to-end.
- Ensure on-call can answer: “is shadow impacting primary?”, “are we dropping shadow?”, “what changed?”, and “how do we disable safely?”

Non-goals
- Designing the shadow runner architecture (tracked in design/ADR).
- Building new telemetry primitives beyond what Telemetry team is already adding; focus is on SRE thresholds/ops readiness.

Acceptance criteria
- Capacity budget doc approved by SRE lead (Sean Gallagher) and Platform Eng lead (Dylan Brooks) with explicit numbers per region/tier.
- Load test plan published (and at least one representative run executed) with results summarized and linked.
- Alert rules merged for: shadow queue depth, shadow error rate, shadow drop counts, and worker saturation signal.
- Runbook verified during a tabletop: kill switch + verification queries + comms steps.
- Beta readiness checklist updated with links and owners.

References / links
- Confluence: shadow SLO impact and budgets (draft): sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/shadow-traffic-slo-impact-and-budgets.json
- Runbook: kill switch: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-shadow-runner-kill-switch.json
- Load test sheet: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/shadow-runner-load-test-plan-sheet.json
- Related work: ENG-2443 (kill switch), ENG-2435 (cardinality guardrails), ENG-2419 (shadow runner execution path)

Proposed initial budgets (to validate via load tests)
- Default sampling cap: 0.5% per route (beta default), hard cap 5% unless explicitly approved.
- Global concurrent shadow executions: cap at 10% of primary concurrency per region (shadow-only pool), or queue-enforced equivalent.
- Queue: target steady-state depth < 2 minutes of work; page if > 10 minutes sustained.
- Drops: allowed; page only if drop rate exceeds threshold over sustained window or correlated with primary regression.

Alerting proposal (initial)
- shadow_queue_depth_seconds (or derived): warn at 300s for 10m; page at 600s for 10m.
- shadow_error_rate: warn at 2% for 15m; page at 5% for 10m (excluding explicit ‘dropped_due_to_budget’).
- shadow_drop_rate_budget: warn at 1% for 10m; page at 5% for 10m (by region).
- shadow_worker_saturation: page if workers at > 90% busy for 15m AND queue depth rising.

Notes
Primary-path guardrail is strict: no measurable primary p99 regression beyond agreed budget attributable to shadow feature. Shadow can fail/timeout/drop; must be isolated and observable.
comments: 2025-10-15 (Sean Gallagher): Creating this as the Beta ops gating item. We need explicit budgets + test results before enabling sampling on any enterprise routes.
2025-10-16 (Vanessa Ortiz): Please include regional caps; EU-WEST is currently tighter on GPU headroom. I can provide baseline utilization numbers for the test windows.

2025-10-17 (Rafael Mendes): Drafting runbook updates. Need confirmation on the exact signals/queries that prove “shadow is not on primary path” (e.g., primary latency panel + shadow queue depth panel side-by-side).
2025-10-21 (Dylan Brooks): +1. Also want this to cover backpressure behavior. If queue saturates, I want to see explicit drop counters (shadow-only) and no cascading retries.
2025-10-24 (Thomas Baird): Reminder: alert dimensions must be low-cardinality. Please don’t page per-route; aggregate by region + service + environment and use dashboards for drill-down.
2025-10-28 (Rafael Mendes): Added alert drafts for queue depth and drop counts. Waiting on final metric names from telemetry PR (ENG-2427/PR-48261).
2025-11-02 (Sean Gallagher): Budget proposal: start beta with 0.5% sampling default + 2% hard cap. Any higher requires SRE approval per region.

2025-11-07 (Rafael Mendes): Ran load test at 0.5%, 1%, 2% sampling in us-east + eu-west. At 2% saw queue depth growth when judge scoring enabled; drop counters engaged as expected. No primary p99 impact observed in the perf canary run (link in sheet).
2025-11-09 (Allison Grant): Alert thresholds look good. Please add a note in the runbook about expected shadow-only error modes (judge timeouts, redact failures) and what NOT to page on.
2025-11-12 (Rafael Mendes): Tabletop complete: kill switch toggled, verified drop to zero shadow executions within ~60s, primary unaffected. Added verification steps + comms checklist to runbook.
2025-11-19 (Sean Gallagher): Approved to mark done once alert rules merged + dashboard links are in runbook and beta checklist.
2025-11-20 (Rafael Mendes): Alerts merged and dashboards linked. Marking Done.
